historical_reviews.v3_1: A BootOptionId is valid only in the selected System's BootOptions collection; the member GET must prove both membership and returned-resource identity.

original_test_intent: Read one real BootOption member belonging to the selected ComputerSystem and validate its identity and option metadata without changing boot configuration.
original_method: Resolve the System and BootOptions collection, select an approved advertised member link, then use trusted curl/jq to GET it once and validate `@odata.id`, option identity, reference/display/enabled/device-path fields and parent association.
manual_activity: Provision the reusable secure Redfish package, target-member selection policy and BootOption schema/redaction rules; no per-run confirmation or manual boot-state action is required afterward.
required_inputs: BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
BootOption member schema and field policy
safety_requirements: Never use literal `ID` as a member
Require the selected member to appear in the parent collection
No PATCH/POST boot change, one-time boot, reboot, power or log clearing
agent_execution_scope: Select exactly one approved member link
Capture status/headers and access-controlled raw hash
Validate returned identity, parent membership and option fields
Export redacted snapshot and no-write/no-reboot audit
engineer_actions: Maintain member-selection, schema and redaction policy

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: curl/jq are suitable, but `/Systems/system/BootOptions/ID` is not a resolved member and `.BootOption` is not an established resource field; the command omits parent-membership and exact identity checks.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With trusted TLS and secret-safe credentials, follow one approved BootOption `Members[].@odata.id` from the selected System's BootOptions collection, GET it once, require matching `@odata.id`/identifier and validate the approved option fields before redacted export.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The single BootOption member GET and 15/10 timing remain; no SystemId, BootOptionId or option field values are guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Chain collection discovery to the member read so the identifier is provenance-bound, then validate resource identity and option metadata with no boot-state mutation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces literal placeholders, fixed System identity, unsafe access and a null-prone filter with advertised-link and member-schema validation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates one selected option member in depth; complete option population remains the preceding collection case's responsibility.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Boot option device paths and references may expose topology and can change across firmware or hardware configuration; selection and redaction policies must be stable and versioned.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish SDK is equivalent only if it preserves the System→BootOptions→member link chain, certificate binding and returned-resource identity. A caller-supplied arbitrary ID cannot replace collection-derived selection.
expected_evidence: Immutable BMC and selected System identity
Validated BootOptions collection and chosen member link
HTTP status/content type and raw response hash
No boot write, reboot, power, firmware or log mutation

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master item and nested URI consistently describe reading a BootOption member identified by BootOptionId. The literal `ID`, fixed SystemId and `.BootOption` projection occur only in DeepSeek's generated command and are review defects rather than Master contradictions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The member operation is explicit and can run deterministically by resolving a member from the preceding collection after standard secure package configuration.

review_improvement: Binds BootOptionId to a real parent collection member and adds exact returned-resource, parent and field validation instead of accepting a placeholder/null result.
independent_technical_reasoning: A syntactically plausible BootOption URI is not proof that the option belongs to the selected System. The identifier must originate from that System's BootOptions `Members` set, and the returned resource must echo the same `@odata.id` or approved identifier. Otherwise a stale, fabricated or cross-System ID could be accepted. Member-level fields must be validated without conflating this case with collection completeness or any write to boot order.
